source.title: Muon Reduces the Training Cost of Regulatory DNA Transformers
source.authors: Viraj M. Doshi; Malhar Bhide; Akshat Singh; Yash M. Rathod; Aditya Sivakumar

record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizer effects on held-out performance in regulatory DNA Transformers, extending optimizer-generalization comparisons to a new domain.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out perplexity and training-loss comparisons across optimizers and norm-control schemes. It does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Appendix G gives final EMA perplexities; figure-only learning curves are not used to infer unreported numerical values.
record.test_reason: The study compares Adam with SGD on held-out regulatory-DNA perplexity under a fixed 20-epoch recipe and learning-rate sweep. This bears on V4 in a new sequence-modeling domain. Muon-versus-Adam efficiency comparisons alone do not test V4's adaptive-versus-SGD claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: MuonW reduces the compute and time needed to reach Adam-matched regulatory-DNA perplexity, and norm control affects optimizer rankings. The proposed spectral explanation is tentative. Results do not establish downstream biological improvements, and the authors acknowledge the fixed recipe, limited scale, and lack of repeated seeds or significance tests.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Muon versus Adam on regulatory DNA Transformers, with optimizer family, norm-control scheme, learning rate, and width varied; the paper holds other stated training factors fixed. It does not reproduce the original image-classification or language benchmarks.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer ranking and training-loss progression depend on learning rate and norm-control scheme; tested model width also changes the median matched-target cost advantage.

fits_no_version.finding: Muon reaches Adam-matched held-out perplexity with 18.3–39.7% fewer FLOPs and 24.6–42.0% less wall-clock time across tested scales, and selected Muon runs achieve lower final EMA perplexity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Muon can improve regulatory-DNA Transformer training efficiency and held-out perplexity relative to Adam under the tested recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Muon-versus-Adam training-loss rankings depend on learning rate and norm control.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer update rules and norm control jointly affect training dynamics in regulatory-DNA Transformers.

fits_no_version.finding: MuonW preserves higher weight participation ratio than the other configurations and has the best held-out perplexity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preserved effective weight rank accompanies better held-out perplexity in this optimizer sweep; causality is not established.

record.problems: The sweep used 90 runs of 20 epochs but did not include multiple seeds for each setting; authors report no error bars or statistical significance tests. Batch size, sequence length, masking setup, architecture, data mixture, and weight decay were held fixed. Models cover up to 420M parameters. Held-out perplexity is the target; downstream biological prediction is not shown.
record.rows_left_out: None. Figure-only learning-curve values were not numerically reconstructed; qualitative results described in the text are recorded in R1, R3, and R5.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out generalization.
Widening beyond zero training error with training to convergence; the width sweep does not establish an interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.

The original image and natural-language benchmarks; broader hyperparameter tuning; recovery through decoupled weight decay or switching from Adam to SGD; whether adaptive methods outperform on training while underperforming on held-out data. The study instead tests regulatory-DNA masked language modeling with fixed norm-control recipes and a learning-rate sweep.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations that remove a large-batch penalty.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its relationship to generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples versus randomly selected examples and retraining.

missing.what: Best final EMA perplexities for Adam versus SGD at each width. Width 512: AdamH 2.5668, AdamW 2.5870, SgdH 2.6402, SgdW 2.7694. Width 1024: AdamH 2.5644, AdamW 2.5825, SgdH 2.6467, SgdW 2.7733. Width 2048: AdamH 2.5579, AdamW 2.5761, SgdH 2.6724, SgdW 2.7743. Add numerical comparison rows for all widths; R3 currently captures only the largest-scale qualitative result.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. Adam beating SGD in this new domain warrants a scope qualification, not support for adaptive methods generalizing worse. No generalization-gap mechanism is established by the Muon efficiency or spectral results.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold and test-error trends.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.

Image-classification and language benchmarks; SGD and momentum SGD comparisons; broader hyperparameter tuning; decoupled weight decay recovery and switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language models.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: Transformer models (26M–420M parameters)
rows.operation_detail: Compared optimizer-family held-out perplexity progression at matched compute and wall-clock budgets.
rows.measure: Held-out perplexity progression and cost to reach matched perplexity targets
rows.baseline: Adam target perplexity and corresponding cost
rows.value: Muon reaches better held-out perplexity over a broad set of budgets; after the earliest targets, its advantage typically falls in the 35–45% range for FLOPs and wall-clock time.
rows.note: Family curves report the best held-out perplexity achieved by any run in each optimizer family.
rows.check: Muon-versus-Adam efficiency does not establish adaptive methods' performance relative to SGD. The 35–45% advantage and Figures 2–3 concern the largest scale, rather than the full 26M–420M range.

rows.subject: Transformer models (26M–420M parameters)
rows.operation_detail: Compared median cost reductions across matched Adam perplexity targets by model scale.
rows.measure: Median reduction in FLOPs and wall-clock time to matched held-out perplexity
rows.baseline: Adam cost to reach each matched perplexity target
rows.value: 18.3–39.7% fewer FLOPs and 24.6–42.0% less wall-clock time across tested scales.
rows.note: The ranges summarize results across the three tested scales.
rows.check: The reported matched-target cost reductions are accurate but compare Muon with Adam, not adaptive methods with SGD.

rows.subject: Transformer models, width 2048
rows.operation_detail: Compared the selected run for each optimizer variant by mean held-out perplexity over training FLOPs.

conditions.value: Run with lowest final EMA perplexity for each optimizer variant

rows.measure: Mean held-out perplexity as a function of training FLOPs
rows.value: The curves separate clearly: SGD remains well above the Adam and Muon variants; the best Muon configuration reaches its lowest perplexity on a smaller compute and wall-clock budget.
rows.note: The paper describes the comparison qualitatively; precise curve values are figure-only.
rows.check: Adam achieves lower held-out perplexity than SGD, reversing the adaptive-worse direction rather than showing it partially. Identify the SGD comparators as SgdH and SgdW; the Muon portion is ancillary.

rows.subject: Transformer models, width 2048
rows.operation_detail: Compared best final-EMA-perplexity runs across optimizer variants in the sweep.
rows.note: Values are the lowest-EMA selected runs in the width 2048 columns; the paper reports that these selections match Figure 5.
rows.check: Muon-versus-Adam endpoints do not test V4. The stated best AdamW value is also incorrect: Appendix G gives 2.5761 at LR 3.6e-04, whereas 2.5931 is a nonminimum entry. The other three reported minima are correct.

rows.subject: Transformer models
rows.operation_detail: Compared training-loss progression across optimizer variants and norm-control schemes.
rows.value: Muon reaches lower training loss than Adam; the reported ranking is MuonW, MuonH, AdamH, then AdamW. Ranking and relative performance depend on learning rate and norm-control scheme.
rows.note: Training-loss curves are described qualitatively; the paper notes learning-rate dependence.
rows.check: Training loss alone cannot establish held-out generalization, and this row contains no SGD comparison. Learning-rate dependence of these training curves does not itself limit V4.

rows.subject: Transformer models, FFN Layer 3
rows.operation_detail: Measured learned weight spectral entropy and normalized participation ratio across optimizer variants.
rows.measure: Weight spectral entropy and normalized participation ratio
rows.baseline: MuonW: approximately 0.95 spectral entropy and approximately 0.57 normalized PR
rows.value: MuonH: approximately 0.93 spectral entropy and approximately 0.46 normalized PR; AdamW: approximately 0.36 normalized PR; AdamH: spectral entropy near 0.87 and PR near 0.14.
rows.note: These measurements concern spectra, not the optimizer generalization comparison named by V4; they are recorded as reported accompanying results, not evidence for a V4 verdict.
rows.check: Weight spectral entropy and participation ratio measure neither adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance nor V7's magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness.

relationships.condition: ENCODE regulatory-DNA masked language modeling; widths 512, 1024, and 2048; 20 epochs; best learning rate per optimizer and norm-control variant
relationships.reason: R3 reports Adam outperforming SGD at width 2048; Appendix G additionally shows both Adam variants beating both SGD variants at every width. This establishes a new domain where the adaptive-worse tendency does not extend; the additional numerical comparisons are missing from the rows.
relationships.display_finding: Reported advantages for both Adam variants over both SGD variants at every tested width remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ENCODE regulatory-DNA pretraining; tested widths and 20-epoch recipe
reader_labels.reason: Muon reaches better held-out perplexity at lower matched cost than Adam (R1, R2); at width 2048 the selected Muon runs also have lower final EMA perplexity than the Adam runs (R4). This extends the optimizer comparison to a domain outside V4's stated benchmarks.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Training loss and optimizer ranking across the tested sweep
reader_labels.reason: Muon's lower training loss and ranking depend on learning rate and norm-control scheme; this is not a general comparison of adaptive methods with SGD under the version's limited-tuning benchmark conditions (R3, R5).
